question: Should OpenClaw add an internal `session:end` hook event, or should workflow integrations use the existing typed plugin `session_end` hook instead?
rationale: Both surfaces can support lifecycle automation, but adding a new internal hook changes the public automation API while the current plugin hook may already be the intended runtime lifecycle contract.

options.title: Approve an internal session:end contract
options.body: Define and document a narrow internal `session:end` event, then implement it consistently across the relevant session completion paths with focused tests.

options.title: Use plugin session_end as the contract
options.body: Document the existing typed plugin `session_end` hook as the supported completion surface for workflow integrations and close or retitle this issue after that decision is visible.

options.title: Wait for linked PR review first
options.body: Keep this issue open until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/61675 is landed or closed, then reassess any remaining internal-hook gap.

recommendation.title: Use plugin session_end as the contract
recommendation.body: Document the existing typed plugin `session_end` hook as the supported completion surface for workflow integrations and close or retitle this issue after that decision is visible.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice is primarily a hook/plugin API-boundary decision and vincentkoc is the strongest recent routing signal in the hook/plugin history and issue timeline.
